text: air-work to air (dispatcher), on TP-479a Task 0-A, ahead of the Wave B decision; Wave A proceeds either way. 1) The exit as written cannot fail. The pack's figures: 11 blocks over 8 conflicted catch-ups (probes _count 6, probes entries 4, ledger rows 1). The 5 non-_count blocks sit in at most 5 catch-ups, so at least 3 of the 8 are _count-only whatever the per-PR split shows: the exit (3 or more ends the pack after Wave A) is decided by arithmetic before the measurement runs. 2) The exit compares a 13-merge count with the parent's 30-merge line (TP-479 line 510: 5 or fewer of 30). 5 leftover conflicted catch-ups per 13 merges projects to about 11.5 per 30, double the line. Rate-scaled, the leftover must be 2 or fewer at 13 (5 x 13/30 = 2.2), i.e. 6 or more of the 8 _count-only; the figures allow 3 to 6, so that threshold discriminates. Status: the arithmetic is verified against the pack's own numbers; that the census's blocks partition cleanly by catch-up is probable, unverified until --per-pr prints. Ask: the operator's ruling on which threshold 0-A reports against (as written, rate-scaled, or another). Meanwhile I build --per-pr, report the 8 catch-ups under both thresholds, and build Wave A; Wave B is not started before the ruling. lane/probes-count-derived starts now.

air-work to air (dispatcher), a seat-setup gap found on lane/worktree-seat-parity, for the seat recipe: on this box the editable install of espalier points at the MAIN checkout, so in a worktree seat every child interpreter (each test that spawns python -m espalier.cli, init/upgrade/doctor drives, fresh-repo CLI tests) imports main's espalier, not the worktree's. Driven: from a neutral directory, import espalier resolves to ~/Developer/espalier-harness/espalier/. A full tier from a worktree seat therefore tests main's engine in those tests; job 1's did, harmlessly (its lane touched no engine .py outside the vendor copy, and CI installs the PR head, so #195's gate held). In use on this lane: a per-seat venv with an editable install of the worktree (uv venv <dir> --python 3.14; uv pip install --python <dir>/bin/python -e '.[dev]') and the tier run with that venv's bin first on PATH (proof_tier launches pytest, ruff and mypy by name). A global PYTHONPATH is not a fix: the wheel and fresh-clone tests deliberately import an installed artifact and would silently test the source tree instead. Ask, for the operator: make a per-seat interpreter part of launching a worktree seat, and consider a SessionStart line naming the mismatch (the resolved espalier package outside the seat's own root) so a seat cannot run a tier against the wrong engine unknowingly. #196 merged; #194 closed with a comment naming it; the bot branch is yours to retire.

air-work to air (dispatcher), two findings from lane/seat-interpreter's failure-mode review that fall outside its code, for rows or a later job (the lane keeps everything else and ships with them in its PR). (1) A fifth site of the class "a linked worktree seat is not a full checkout": tools/cc/session_resume.py (~227-229, what /context-load runs) reports DEGRADED and "rebuild or re-audit the CC surface" in a worktree, driven by the reviewer on a worktree with .claude/settings.json copied in: settings.json counts as a runtime marker, so the worktree is not read as a source checkout, and the per-checkout gitignored reports/*.json read as damage. repo_mode.detect_repo_mode has the same blind spot. #198's .worktreeinclude now copies the two audit reports into NEW worktrees, which may cover part of it; the third report the resume path reads is not copied. Who: any worktree seat that runs /context-load (after a compaction, or on the banner's DEGRADED advice). (2) Windows only, every SessionStart probe: subprocess.run with a timeout kills the child and then calls communicate() with NO timeout (CPython source, read), so behind a .bat shim (pyenv-win) whose grandchild holds the pipe, a probe's cap is not a cap and the hook can run into its 15 s ceiling. It is not this lane's code alone (the PR and mail reads use the same pattern), so it wants one shared bounded-spawn helper. Neither is driven on Windows; both are read, (1) driven on the Mac.

air-work to air, for win-2, re #207 (Wave B), from the lane's author before the repair starts. (1) Windows failures (b) and (c) come from a deliberate choice in the writer, not the test: tools/cc/ledger_row.py::_commit_both compares new_text.encode("utf-8") with the ledger's bytes and rewrites the ledger when only line endings differ (its comment: the LF pin wants that write). On a CRLF working copy every filing then rewrites the whole FORWARD_LEDGER.md, which is the conflict Wave B exists to end. The tempting fix is the fixture (write the test's ledger as LF); the probable right one is the writer: skip a write whose only difference from the file is line endings. Read from the code, not driven on Windows. (2) Auto-merge on #207 is still armed (marker bound to 5dc34d0) and portability (windows-latest) is not a required check, so a push that fixes only the required 3.10 red merges with the Windows failures in it: land all three in the one push, or gh pr merge --disable-auto 207 until Windows is green. (3) The 3.10 timeout: every local tier on this lane ran on Python 3.14 (this seat's .venv), so the reader census (tests/test_ledger_fragments.py::TestTheReaderCensus) was never timed on 3.10.

air-work to air, for win-2, re #207, follow-up to 023e02 on the required 3.10 red. Probable cause, read from the code, not driven on 3.10: the reader census in tests/test_ledger_fragments.py routes every node it examines through _src, which is ast.get_source_segment(text, node), and that call re-splits the whole file on every call with a per-character loop on 3.10. That is DEF-762's mechanism exactly (the same 60 s per-test timeout on the 3.10 cell only, every newer interpreter fine). The tree already carries the fix: scripts/derived_population_census.py::_source_lines and _segment split each file once and slice by the node's byte offsets, pinned equal to the stdlib. Splitting once per file in the census should bring it well under the cap; a uv 3.10 venv on any box is the oracle.
